content.question: What is the difference between a core point and a border point in DBSCAN?
options: A core point has the minimum number of points at distance epsilon from itself, while a border point lies within epsilon of core points but lacks enough neighbours to be called core itself.
A core point belongs to the largest cluster, while a border point belongs to the smallest one.
A core point is chosen randomly at the start, while a border point is the last point added to the cluster.
A core point has no neighbours at all, while a border point has exactly K neighbours.
content.answer: A core point has the minimum number of points at distance epsilon from itself, while a border point lies within epsilon of core points but lacks enough neighbours to be called core itself.
